example:
In a shallow clone with no history beyond the last commit, each window holds
only the files' contents on disk and in that commit. `habeas status` says that
coverage history is incomplete and warns about items those contents do not
cover. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
rationale:
The example's scenario is a shallow clone with only the last commit. In that clone, `habeas status` must say coverage history is incomplete and must warn about items the available contents do not cover. Three tests in `tests/coverage.rs` carry a `{test}` reference to the example and cover this.

- `a_shallow_clone_uses_the_history_it_has_and_says_so`: The setup records `rules.check` reading `fn[parse]` and commits it. It then records an empty `rules.check`, commits again, and runs `git clone --depth 1`. In the clone it asserts that `coverage_warning_lines` contains "coverage history is incomplete". It also asserts that `warned(&target)` is `["parse","render","helper"]`. So `parse` is warned because the only commit available no longer reads it. The full-history repo yields only `["render","helper"]`, which shows the shallow window really is limited to what is available.
- `status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete`: It builds the same two-commit history and checks that the non-shallow `status_markdown` has no "history is incomplete" text. In the `--depth 1` clone, `status_markdown` contains "Coverage history is incomplete" and "function parse has no recent coverage". This covers both expected `status` outcomes: the incompleteness statement and the warning for items the available contents do not cover.
- `incomplete_history_is_noted_even_with_nothing_to_warn_about`: In a shallow clone it asserts that the incompleteness line is the only warning line and appears in `status_markdown`. It also asserts that the full repo has none. This confirms the note is independent of the item warnings.

The `project`, `record`, `commit` and `warned` helpers build a real Git repo with evidence files that name outline nodes, so the scenario is exercised through real Git clones and not through mocks. The tests call `status_markdown`, the library function behind `habeas status`, and I did not read that function's body. No gaps were found.

In a shallow clone with no history beyond the last commit, each window holds
only the files' contents on disk and in that commit. `habeas status` says that
coverage history is incomplete and warns about items those contents do not
cover. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
:::{req} coverage.history
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
